title: Tension a messenger wire and hang its ring at the mark
instruction: Tension the black messenger wire by moving its end block into the far notch of the grey bracket, and leave the orange hanger ring hanging on the wire right above the red mark. Let go of both.
context: Line installers "string cables between structures and lines from poles, towers, or trenches, and pull lines to proper tension" (O*NET 49-9052.00). Hardware then rides the installed line: "All stringing blocks should be placed on the steel messenger facing the same direction" (OCC aerial lashing guide OCC-206-6). Here drawing the wire tight drags the ring ~7 cm, so hold it during tensioning or place it after.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). A 5 mm black wire (light coated cord, 10 g) runs along y at x 30, 9 up, out of a dark grey anchor post (4 wide, y -30 to -20, 10.8 tall; 12 mm channel at wire height, spring tensioner inside: 0.2 N at rest, 1.0 N with 8 cm out). It ends in a black ferrule block (30x20x20 mm, 5 g) in the near notch (centre y 12) of a grey bracket (6 wide, y 9-23.8, 8 tall). Far notch: y 18.2-22.6. Each notch has a cross wall (6 mm thick, 15 mm tall) with a 9 mm wire slit; a 4 mm tall, 6 mm wide lip runs along each long edge of the bracket top, and the far notch ends in a similar end wall. Orange printed square ring (35 mm wide, 25 mm opening, 5x8 mm bars, 35x8x16 mm grab plate on top, 5 g) hangs on the wire at y -4. Red tape mark, 6x0.8, on the table under the wire at y -13.
scoring: Score 0 if: the ferrule is not resting on the floor of the far notch; the wire sags more than 10 mm below the straight line between post and bracket; the ring is off the wire (its centre more than 2 cm from the wire) or tilted over 45 deg; a gripper is within 3 cm of the ferrule, ring or wire at the end; in a real trial, the post or bracket is moved. Otherwise, by the ring centre's distance along the wire from the mark: within 10 mm = 1.0; within 25 mm = 0.5; farther = 0. Success when 1.0 holds for 1 s with the ring at rest.
reset_notes: Put the ferrule back in the near notch (the spring takes the wire back into the post) and slide the ring back to y -4 cm, 16 cm from the post face.
fidelity: Scale model of a messenger: light cord and about 1 N, not steel at working tension. Wire: rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no stretch or twist. The tensioner is a linear spring on the wire's hidden end (10 N/m, 10 cm stop). The ring is five welded bars, one printed part in reality, and rides the wire by contact friction, so its drag under tensioning depends on friction. Sag is read from segment centres; a real trial uses a straight edge.
